title: Doc Ryker's tapes, their romance, and the gabfest at Virginia's
summary: The Ryker tapes led to Chauncey and Virginia seeing each other; he came down from New York and Paul Mertz and others stayed at her house.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And from that, of course we were so intrigued. Doc Ryker had been interviewing the different men. He had the tapes. The men who were with the Goldkette band.
I've got a set of the tapes.
You have?
What became of Goldkette? "What's Left of Goldkett" is the name of the tapes.
And of course we heard Chauncey on the tape. And we heard all these fellows on the tape. We were so intrigued. We had to go, you know.
That's great.
And out of that came our little romance.
That's fantastic.
Isn't it something. The Donoho's, they were so proud to think that we were there.
Did they invite you to go there?

They brought us together, you know. It was just one of the most memorable evenings you could have ever imagined. And of course Chauncey was up there in the bar. And he was just beating it out. And I was just glowing. Oooh isn't he cute.
Oh that's great.

But then disaster fell upon us, you know in just a few months. Almost gone one of us... In August we met, I think it was. I don't remember the exact date of that meeting at Donoho's. And the Rykers came back. And then we had called Chauncey because, well just out of pure intrigue. So he came down from New York. And we had a marvelous gabfest here. And Paul Hertz, I forgot about him.
Paul Mertz came.
Paul Mertz, he and Florence came here. I had a house full and they all stayed, you know.
Wow, wow!
We had such a great time. And those that ever thought of taping all that.
That was marvelous, yes.
It was just a fantastic meeting with us all.
That was terrific.
